description.value:
A self-custody crypto wallet for people who take security seriously. Your BIP-39 recovery phrase is your identity and keys never leave the device. No custody, no email login, no backdoor — and no way for anyone, including us, to move your funds without your PIN and your device.

TEN ASSETS, EIGHT NETWORKS, ONE SEED:
• Ethereum (ETH), Polygon (MATIC), Arbitrum (ARB), Optimism (OP), Avalanche (AVAX), BNB Smart Chain (BNB)
• Bitcoin (BTC), native SegWit
• Solana (SOL)
• USDC and USDT
One address for the EVM chains, dedicated addresses for Bitcoin and Solana.

THEFT PROTECTION (NEW)
An optional extra check for a stolen, unlocked phone. Unlocking asks for Face ID after your PIN — and again on a send over your spend limit, or when you raise that limit or turn the protection off. On iPhone this is Face ID specifically — a Touch-ID-only device cannot enrol. We store no biometric data; the check is a yes-or-no answer from the operating system. It stays silent in decoy and hidden sessions, so a forced unlock never reveals it is on.

RUNTIME SELF-PROTECTION
Veyrnox checks its own runtime for tampering, jailbreaking, code injection, and hooking, and fails closed on a compromised device.

ADDRESS SAFETY
Poisoning and look-alike address warnings, plus spam-token filtering, before you send.

BUY CRYPTO
Fund your wallet with card, bank transfer, or Apple Pay via Transak. Checkout opens in a secure system browser and hands you back to the app when it finishes. Rates and fees are shown before you commit; your crypto lands in your own wallet, never a custodial account.

STEP-BY-STEP SEND
Recipient, amount, review, confirm — one decision at a time, with plain-language fees, spend limits, and a clear statement that a transfer cannot be undone.

WALLETCONNECT v2
Pair by QR or link. Every session, signature, and token approval is explained in plain language before you sign — token, spender, exact amount, and whether it is unlimited — with chain and address binding, session expiry, and step-up re-auth for high-risk actions.

AI SECURITY ADVISOR
Answers questions about scams, phishing, seed-phrase hygiene, and safe signing. It is the one feature that talks to a server: questions go to our threat-intelligence service over an encrypted connection, and you opt in first. Fed a weekly digest of vendor advisories and known-bad addresses and contracts.

HARDWARE-BACKED ENCRYPTION
AES-256-GCM with Argon2id key derivation. On supported devices an additional hardware key is bound to the Secure Enclave, so the vault cannot be unlocked on another device even if the encrypted blob is copied.

FAST UNLOCK
Face ID prompts automatically on the lock screen, with a fast path that keeps unlock under a second on modern iPhones — without weakening the crypto underneath.

COERCION-RESISTANT DESIGN
For the reality that someone might force you to open the app. A deniable mode shows a plausible empty wallet. A duress PIN opens a decoy vault. A panic gesture wipes local state. In these modes the app makes zero backend calls and leaves no residue for a later inspection.

PERSONAL BACKUP (2-OF-3)
Split your recovery into three shards with Shamir's Secret Sharing. Any two restore the wallet; one alone reveals nothing.

REAL-TIME PRICES
Live 24-hour price movement on every asset, from public feeds. No ads.

OPTIONAL SUBSCRIPTIONS
Safety Plus ($5.99/mo, $49.99/yr): Personal Backup, duress PIN, hidden wallets, panic wipe.
AI Security Protection ($19.99/mo, $159.99/yr): Safety Plus plus Live Vigil, a TIP-backed AI security chat.
Monthly or annual; auto-renews until cancelled. Manage or cancel in your App Store account settings.

PRIVACY
Anonymous usage events are sent only if you opt in on first launch, and can be turned off in Settings → Privacy. Nothing you type — no seed, no PIN, no address book — ever leaves your device. Privacy policy: veyrnox.com/privacy

You own the seed. If you lose your recovery phrase, no one — including us — can restore your wallet.

whatsNew.value:
Theft Protection (optional)
An extra biometric check when you unlock, and again on a send that goes over your spend limit. It is now also required to loosen a spend limit or switch the protection off. On iPhone this is Face ID specifically. On Android it is any strong biometric: Android provides no way to require face alone, so we do not claim it does.

You can see what you are approving
When an app asks to spend your tokens over WalletConnect, the screen now names the token, the spender and whether the amount is unlimited. Several approval types previously showed only a raw code and "Value: 0".

Referral links that survive an install
Tap an invite link, choose "Copy code & get it on the App Store", then after installing paste it into "Have a referral code?" and tap Apply. Your code is applied when you finish setup.

Also fixed
Redeem Code and Manage Subscription open properly; they previously did nothing. The send amount is larger and is actually applied. A spend limit can be adjusted. The send screen says plainly that a transfer cannot be undone. Bigger tap targets, a readable minimum text size, and clearer empty screens throughout.
whatsNew.note: Source of truth for the 1.0.2 release notes; every sibling locale is machine-translated from this string. `reviewed` stays true here because this file is the source — there is no translation fidelity to vouch for. Corrected 2026-09-19 after the #2541 iOS fresh-install run: the referral paragraph described the Android mechanism ("the code is still applied afterwards"), which is automatic only via Play Install Referrer. iOS needs Copy code -> Paste -> Apply, and apple.whatsNew is read only by iOS users. play.releaseNotes was accurate and is unchanged. All 43 siblings re-translated from this string in the same commit.

Theft Protection: an optional extra biometric check when you unlock, and again on a send over your spend limit.
Privacy: decoy and hidden sessions no longer read or change analytics, budgets, recurring payments, savings goals or invoices. Panic wipe clears two markers it was missing.
Referral links now survive an install.

releaseNotes.note: Play caps release notes at 500 chars (Apple allows 4000), so this is its own shorter string, not a truncation of apple.whatsNew.
